MSTR Technical Outlook: Key Levels and Trend Signals

Technically, the stock is pressing into a key long-term inflection area: it’s trading right on top of its 200-day simple moving average ($139.32), a level that often acts like a "line in the sand" for trend followers. It’s also trading 23.1% above the 20-day SMA ($113.11) and 36.2% above the 50-day SMA ($102.24), which shows the recent rebound has been forceful.

Momentum looks improved using MACD as the primary lens: MACD is above its signal line and the histogram is positive, which points to easing downside pressure versus the prior downswing. That said, the longer-term backdrop still carries baggage because the 50-day SMA remains below the 200-day SMA (a Death Cross that formed in October 2025), so bulls typically want to see sustained trade above the 200-day before calling it a full trend reset.
Key Resistance
: $149.50 — Nearby ceiling that lines up as the next obvious pivot area above the 200-day zone
Key Support
: $118.50 — Prior buyer area that also sits near the 20-day EMA ($117.61), making it a practical "first support" on pullbacks
MSTR Outperforms as Technology Sector Rallies

Strategy is outperforming its sector sharply today, up 13.13% versus a 1.15% gain for Technology — an 11.98%-point gap that puts the move well beyond what you’d expect from simple sector drift. Technology ranks third out of 11 sectors today, so the tape is supportive, but Strategy is still doing the heavy lifting on its own.

Zooming out, the sector has been choppy: down 0.68% over the past 30 days but up 2.96% over the past 90 days, which fits a "two steps forward, one step back" trend. In that context, Strategy’s ability to reclaim the 200-day area matters because it can shift the conversation from "bounce" to "trend repair" if it holds.
